newsitem.title: UK: British management buy-outs at record levels - KPMG.
newsitem.headline: British management buy-outs at record levels - KPMG.

text.p: Management buy-outs in Britain hit record levels in the first quarter of this year, unhampered by the impending election, buy-out advisers KPMG Corporate Finance said on Wednesday.

KPMG said the value of management buy-outs and buy-ins reached 1.97 billion stg in the first quarter, up 42 percent on the year-earlier quarter. If the trend continued, last year's 6.79 billion stg record could be surpassed in 1997.

"Some in the market had expected deals to dry up as the election approached but the tap is still firmly on. Venture capital houses remain flush with cash and are competing fiercely to do deals," Mike Stevens, head of MBO services at KPMG Corporate Finance, said in a statement.
KPMG said 29 deals were worth more than 10 million stg, a record for the traditionally quiet first quarter.

KPM said the largest deals were the 476 million stg buy-out of Granada Group Plc's Welcome Break, the 260 million MBO of Castle Transmission Services and the 150 million acquisition of Birmingham International Airport.
The first quarter was also marked by the first case in recent years of a successful MBO bid in a contested takeover -- the 103 million stg purchase of William Cook Plc.
Stevens said, however, he believed the William Cook deal was a one-off.
"There are unlikely to be many occasions when financial investors are prepared to pay a premium to market price to win a buy-out in a contested takeover situation," he said.
